scope: Normalized repair-readiness supplement for FIN-001..FIN-013 and FIN-CAND-EMPLOYEE-PAYROLL-OVERLAP-001. Derived only from existing canonical source_record details and linked saved evidence; no source reread or shared registry edits.

candidates.title: Mixed cash/electronic checkout cannot confirm its electronic leg
candidates.impact: Mixed cash/electronic checkout can post the immediate tender but reject confirmation of the deferred electronic leg because both paths claim the same completed sale journal key; electronic collection may remain unconfirmed.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Journal idempotency per stable payment-leg identity. Atomically transition pending electronic leg to confirmed and post exactly one leg movement; preserve whole-order and replay semantics without deleting an existing journal as a workaround.
regression_tests: Mixed cash+InstaPay and card+Wallet checkout, confirmation, retry, and concurrent confirm; verify exact tender totals and one movement per leg.
Replay same request and verify stable movement identity.
acceptance_criteria: Each tender leg can complete independently and exactly once.
Confirmed electronic state and its movement commit atomically; channel totals reconcile.
counterevidence: Canonical record says mixed split makes DefersAllMoney false; existing confirmation integration covers only single InstaPay.
No runtime reproduction in saved evidence.
candidates.unresolved_owner_policy: No explicit owner-policy decision identified in the linked canonical record; source record is insufficient to invent one.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Cancelling pending mixed electronic payment hides collected cash without reversal
candidates.impact: Cancelling an order with an already-collected immediate split leg can mark whole order cancelled and remove it from sales reporting while leaving collected cash without reversal, making drawer/revenue totals inconsistent.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Model tender-leg cancellation/outstanding replacement; or require approved refund/reversal for already collected legs before full order cancellation. Keep collected cash represented until a real reversal; state explicit inventory waste policy.
regression_tests: Cancel cash+electronic and card+electronic orders; reconcile treasury, operational cash, and reports.
Race cancel against confirm and require one terminal tender outcome.
Verify refund only when funds are actually returned.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelled order/payment state preserves every collected tender until a matching reversal exists.
Order, tender, treasury, and report totals reconcile after either winning race.
counterevidence: Current integration cancel helper creates only single InstaPay; it does not exercise mixed split.
Inventory non-reversal may be deliberate legacy policy and is outside core cash issue.
unresolved_owner_policy: Confirm intended cancellation/refund semantics for immediate collected legs and inventory waste.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Refund can debit money for an order that was never collected
candidates.impact: Refund handler can use order total less prior refunds rather than settled collection provenance, allowing an authorized refund against an unpaid/pending order if source path permits; pooled account balance only ensures liquidity, not collection.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Derive refundable limit from settled tender legs less prior refunds; require source collection proof. Route pending orders through cancellation. Revalidate under the same order lock and reject unpaid refunds in the domain invariant.
regression_tests: Unpaid COD, pending electronic, confirmed paid, partial collected, and unsupported mixed cases.
Race refund with cancel/confirm and concurrent refunds; rejected cases create no refund/movement and balances remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Cumulative refunds never exceed the order’s actually settled amount per tender leg.
Rejected unpaid refund leaves no partial writes; valid refund atomically records refund and outflow.
counterevidence: Approval permission does not prove collection. Pooled protected balance checks cash availability only. Multi case already rejected; paid single-method refund remains supported.
candidates.unresolved_owner_policy: No explicit owner-policy decision identified in the linked canonical record; source record is insufficient to invent one.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Historical cash refund omitted from current-shift expected cash
candidates.impact: A cash refund executed during current shift B for a sale from shift A may reduce lifetime/order net while the drawer reconciliation for B omits the refund outflow or allocates it to the original sale; expected cash and actual drawer diverge.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Compute drawer flow from posted operational cash movements or join refund rows by OperationalShiftId; avoid double deduction for same-shift refunds and preserve immutable closed shift snapshots. Separate original sale period from refund execution period.
regression_tests: Historical shift A sale refunded in B; verify B actual/expected and final close balance reconcile.
Same-shift partial cash refund counted exactly once.
Historic noncash refund and cross-business-day reports preserve attribution; idempotent retry.
acceptance_criteria: Each refund cash outflow appears once in the shift/business period in which it was executed.
Historical closed shift snapshot remains immutable; current operational drawer reconciles to movements.
counterevidence: Refund rules explicitly promise historical immutability and current shift is required. Existing domain test checks operational shift selection but not reconciliation composition.
unresolved_owner_policy: Confirm report presentation of original sale period versus refund execution period if business reports aggregate them differently.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Concurrent distinct invoice settlements can overpay supplier and corrupt invoice cache
candidates.impact: Two distinct authorized settlements can each read the same invoice outstanding and overpay supplier; invoice cache may then diverge from ledger. Source-account locking can preserve cash solvency while invoice obligation is exceeded.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Within one transaction lock the invoice row before loading outstanding and tracked balance, recompute from supplier-invoice ledger under that lock, validate and atomically post settlement/cache. Define stable invoice/account/approval lock order; retain request idempotency.
regression_tests: Barrier: two different 80 settlements against outstanding 100, both same account and different accounts; at most one succeeds, total <=100 and cache equals ledger.
Same request replay returns committed result.
acceptance_criteria: For each invoice, committed settlements never exceed current outstanding.
Cached paid/outstanding fields match ledger under serialized settlements.
Retries remain idempotent and deadlock policy is bounded.
counterevidence: Treasury lock protects pooled source balance but not invoice freshness. Distinct request IDs legitimately bypass same-key idempotency. No race was executed.
candidates.unresolved_owner_policy: No explicit owner-policy decision identified in the linked canonical record; source record is insufficient to invent one.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Generic payroll transition marks run Paid without paying treasury or employee ledger
candidates.impact: Generic status transition can label an approved payroll run Paid without dedicated payout’s treasury movement and employee ledger settlement; status is not proof of disbursement.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Reject Paid as a generic transition target. Only the dedicated payout command can set Paid after atomically persisting treasury movement, journal, employee settlements, paid lines and audit; coordinate with cancel transition using a run-level lock/CAS.
regression_tests: Generic Approved->Paid is rejected and writes nothing.
Dedicated pay atomically creates expected movement and each settlement.
Actor without payroll_pay cannot set Paid through generic route.
Concurrent cancel/pay results in exactly one consistent terminal state.
acceptance_criteria: Paid status is equivalent to completed committed payout effects.
No API path can mark paid without required payroll_pay authorization and all financial rows.
counterevidence: Dedicated payroll payout path exists. UI narrower next-status list is not server-side guard; canonical record cites route accepting arbitrary status string.
candidates.unresolved_owner_policy: No explicit owner-policy decision identified in the linked canonical record; source record is insufficient to invent one.

candidates.title: Backup filenames collide within a second and WITH FORMAT can overwrite prior backup
candidates.impact: Two backup creations within timestamp resolution can target the same physical filename; later WITH FORMAT may overwrite a previously recorded backup or fail, while retention may count multiple records for one path.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Use collision-resistant immutable backup identity and exclusive create/no-overwrite destination semantics; preserve record-to-file identity. Retention should validate distinct canonical paths and never delete a file still referenced by a retained record.
regression_tests: Parallel same-time filename generation returns distinct IDs/paths.
Existing destination collision refuses overwrite.
Retention with duplicate path references preserves all retained valid backups.
Later isolated SQL/media test only with explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Each successful backup record resolves to a unique immutable artifact.
A collision cannot silently overwrite a prior artifact; retention cannot delete a retained target.
counterevidence: SQL concurrency could cause one backup failure rather than overwrite; either violates an unconditional no-collision guarantee. Physical behavior not runtime-tested.
candidates.unresolved_owner_policy: No explicit owner-policy decision identified in the linked canonical record; source record is insufficient to invent one.

candidates.title: Restore pending-journal check does not exclude active or newly accepted financial work
candidates.impact: Restore’s pending-journal check does not exclude active or newly accepted writes. Restore may enter SINGLE_USER/replace while acknowledged financial operation or background writer is in flight; recovery of latest acknowledged work is not assured by the current check.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Use a database-backed maintenance admission lease respected by all mutating handlers and background workers; drain in-flight operations, pause workers, take safety backup, restore and verify, clear stale pools/caches/sessions as designed, then resume only after durable outcome recording.
regression_tests: Pure coordinator test: after maintenance lease acquired, new writes are rejected and prior writes drained.
Dedicated disposable instance restore with approved fault injection and proof of last acknowledged sale recovery.
Exercise job/API writers and restore failures; never use user-active database.
acceptance_criteria: Restore cannot begin until writers are excluded/drained.
Every accepted operation is either included in pre-restore safety point or has an explicit replay/recovery record.
Failure leaves a known healthy database and maintenance mode controlled.
counterevidence: SINGLE_USER rollback eventually excludes connections but only after the gap; does not prove safe quiescence. Existing source candidate says no runtime test.
unresolved_owner_policy: Define deployment maintenance ownership, writer inventory, recovery point and restore failure/resume procedure before implementation.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Concurrent different open-day requests create multiple active business days
candidates.impact: Concurrent requests with distinct open-day IDs can both pass read-before-write admission, leaving multiple active business days; queries/gates selecting first active day may attach new finance to inconsistent periods.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Represent single active ownership with a database-enforced singleton/unique active-state key acquired transactionally by open and reopen. Reconcile existing duplicate active rows explicitly before constraint migration; make read gate fail closed if invariant is corrupt.
regression_tests: Concurrent opens with distinct IDs: exactly one active day; same request replay returns same day.
Race reopen versus open; exactly one active day.
Corrupt duplicate fixture makes gate fail closed and emits diagnosable error.
acceptance_criteria: At most one active day exists across app processes.
Open/reopen admission and all active-day readers use the same ownership invariant.
counterevidence: Unique OpenRequestId handles only same-request replay, not distinct commands; no database race run.
unresolved_owner_policy: Specify whether Closing and Reopened count as active for ownership and gate semantics before defining index/predicate.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Collected sales report drops immediate money from pending mixed payments
candidates.impact: Sales report may subtract full order amount while an electronic leg is pending even though immediate cash/card leg was collected, understating collected sales/revenue and contradicting channel reconciliation.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Compute pending collection as the pending leg amount(s) and separately report gross/net sale recognition from tender settlement timing. Do not infer collection solely from order IsPaid or subtract whole order for partial pending tender.
regression_tests: Mixed cash/electronic and card/electronic pending: collected amount equals immediate leg and pending equals deferred leg.
After confirm, totals conserve order amount across channels.
Compare report totals to treasury movements and payment query for each state.
acceptance_criteria: For each order, collected plus pending amounts reconcile to eligible tender total; no collected leg disappears while another awaits confirmation.
counterevidence: Idempotency and unrelated locks do not address report arithmetic. Saved evidence is static; no financial writes.
unresolved_owner_policy: Confirm whether report metric is cash collected or accrual sales revenue; keep the two metrics explicitly separate if both are required.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Shift opening and purchase receipt check protected account balance before their transactions
candidates.impact: Shift opening float and/or purchase receipt may authorize against stale Main account balance because protective lock query occurs before transaction; competing outflow may spend same available funds, potentially allowing negative pooled account or failed/partial admission.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Start transaction before protected account balance load/check and hold lock through float/receipt writes; establish consistent account/shift/invoice lock order; make retries safe and preserve real concurrency errors.
regression_tests: Barrier-controlled open-float versus withdrawal/expense/purchase distinct requests; account never negative and exactly feasible operation set commits.
Same open request replay and single-active-shift invariant still hold.
Verify purchase receipt document/inventory/financial rows atomic.
acceptance_criteria: Protected balance read and spend are in one transaction with effective lock lifetime.
No successful concurrent commits exceed available balance; rejected command has no partial effects.
counterevidence: Normal routes have no ambient transaction; an explicit caller transaction could change lock lifetime but is not present in routed path. Same request idempotency and single-open shift do not serialize distinct spends.
unresolved_owner_policy: Confirm supported database provider and transaction/lock strategy before implementation.
candidates.limitations: Existing canonical source-record excerpts and linked saved evidence only; no live source reread, hashes recomputed, tests, runtime, or database operations in this supplement.

candidates.title: Attendance correction credits do not enter calculated payroll
candidates.impact: A positive attendance correction recorded as Adjustment credit may be ignored by payroll’s included earnings/deduction categories, so the corrected employee period net can remain lower than ledger balance.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Reconcile both credit and debit sides of Adjustment into payroll net; preserve correction attribution and original earning basis if required; keep payroll freeze semantics explicit.
regression_tests: Payroll input with prior Deduction debit plus correcting Adjustment credit restores expected net.
Attendance correction followed by payroll calculation and report agrees with employee ledger.
Correction before run creation and after run freeze follow documented policy.
acceptance_criteria: Every eligible period employee-ledger credit/debit included exactly once in payroll liability.
Payroll line and ledger are consistent; post-freeze correction follows explicit reopen/adjustment policy.
counterevidence: Correction must be within period before run creation for current flow; frozen lines after creation are separate. CreatePayroll passes type/credit/debit through unchanged per saved challenge.
unresolved_owner_policy: Specify handling for corrections posted after payroll run calculation/approval: reopen, delta adjustment, or next-period treatment.

candidates.title: Owner dashboard adds outgoing stock instead of subtracting it
candidates.impact: Owner dashboard may add positive-magnitude Out movements to stock total rather than subtracting them, overstating stock and misclassifying low-stock items.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Use shared signed stock-balance rule or apply direction sign in query projection; align dashboard with inventory overview and count-adjustment/waste semantics.
regression_tests: Seed positive-magnitude In and Out movements plus count adjustments/waste; dashboard balance and low-stock set equal inventory overview.
Cover zero/negative normalized inputs and multiple movement kinds.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard stock projection equals canonical inventory balance for every item.
Out never increases available quantity; count corrections are treated per shared domain rule.
counterevidence: Canonical record says InventoryRules and pure tests establish positive Out magnitudes; independent challenge was not saved on legacy record. A related later inventory dashboard challenge exists but is distinct in ID.

candidates.title: Standalone employee settlements are not netted from frozen period payroll
candidates.impact: If standalone Settlement is a prepayment of earnings already included in the same frozen payroll, paying both paths can disburse the same obligation twice; source flow shows this mechanism but does not establish the accounting policy or an actual duplicate payout.
candidates.proposed_remediation: Owner decision first. If settlements prepay same-period earnings, derive remaining liability from an explicit period/earning obligation and apply settlements both before payroll calculation and after run freeze; if the two paths are mutually exclusive, enforce atomic exclusion on both. Preserve frozen-run, replay, audit, source-balance, and historical-record behavior.
regression_tests: Create earnings, settle same obligation standalone, then create/approve/pay payroll; total disbursement must satisfy owner-approved invariant.
Create/approve payroll, apply standalone settlement, then pay frozen payroll; same invariant.
Unrelated-period settlement must not be netted.
Repeat and concurrent requests with distinct IDs; validate exactly-once employee ledger and treasury effects in approved disposable SQL Server integration DB.
acceptance_criteria: Written owner policy defines relationship between standalone Settlement and period payroll obligation.
Tests implement that policy across both sequence orders, period boundaries, retries and concurrent requests.
No duplicate obligation disbursement if policy treats Settlement as prepayment; otherwise distinct obligation is explicitly represented and reported.
counterevidence: Standalone PayEmployee locks employee ledger balance and atomically posts Settlement plus treasury movement.
Code comments describe a separate any-time payment mode, which may imply intentional independence.
Payroll calculation omits Settlement and PayPayroll pays frozen NetPayable, but absence in reviewed paths does not establish system-wide policy or all-path exclusivity.
Coordinator cross-check expressly keeps duplicate payment conditional and reports no combined SQL/runtime sequence.
unresolved_owner_policy: Is standalone employee Settlement a prepayment against earnings included in period payroll, or a distinct payable obligation?
If it is a prepayment, how should settlement after payroll freeze affect already-approved NetPayable: block, adjust/reopen, or record a separate recovery?
candidates.limitations: Source-confirmed flow and atomicity only; policy, actual sequence, SQL/provider behavior and duplicate-payment realization unverified. Do not promote to confirmed duplicate-payment defect.
